reasoning_note: FTP from clinical subnet to external IP at 2 AM is very suspicious, could be data exfiltration of patient records.
Billing user accessing 47 records late at night seems excessive but I'm not sure what normal billing volume looks like so escalating.
Admin VLAN talking to medical devices over SMB should not be happening, could be lateral movement toward patient care equipment.
Lab system pushing 340 MB via SFTP to an external IP that looks like a known Tor exit node range, treating as active exfiltration.
Infusion pump reaching out to an external IP is terrifying from a patient safety standpoint even if severity score is low.
High volume DNS from a medical device could be DNS tunneling or just a misconfigured device, need to check query logs.
Nurse accessing records across three departments at 2:30 AM is unusual, could be snooping or compromised credentials.
ICMP sweep across multiple VLANs from management VLAN looks like reconnaissance, possibly an attacker mapping the network.
RDP from admin to device subnet on a Saturday morning is unusual, could be legitimate maintenance but I'd rather escalate.
Large PACS transfer to external IP could be a teleradiology service but 4.8 GB is a lot and I can't verify the destination.
2.3 GB leaving the PACS archive at 4 AM to an external IP is suspicious, same source as alert A-14 which makes it worse.
Unknown wireless device communicating with hospital IoT on proprietary protocol with severity 8.0 screams rogue device.
Service account pulling 312 records across all departments in 8 minutes at 1 AM is almost certainly a compromised account or insider threat.
A ventilator using Telnet is a huge patient safety risk, Telnet is unencrypted and should never be on life-critical equipment.
EHR to backup server over SMB at 2:30 PM could be a scheduled backup but 28 GB is large and I want to confirm it's legit.
890 MB leaving the pharmacy system on a Saturday at 3 AM to an external IP, don't know if pharmacy has scheduled uploads so escalating.
Patient monitor with 5x normal traffic at 3 AM could be a malfunctioning device or something worse, need to check with biomed.
The EHR server itself is port scanning all internal subnets at 3 AM, this is textbook compromised server behavior and needs immediate isolation.
Physician accessing 22 records from home VPN in the evening seems like normal on-call behavior but will keep an eye on it.
1.1 GB leaving a nurse station in 3 minutes to an external IP is massive data exfiltration, need to pull that workstation off the network now.

q21_note: These alerts are all network-level data with IPs and ports, a nurse or doctor would have no idea what patient safety risk exists without translation into clinical terms.
